## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD-level design and debugging of StatefulSets, bootstrapping, and network policies under real constraints.

## Key Concepts
- StatefulSet with stable identity and PVC
- headless Service and partitioned rolling updates
- InitContainer for bootstrapping
- PodDisruptionBudget and readiness/liveness probes
- Resource quotas and NetworkPolicy bounds

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: cache-svc
  labels:
    app: cache
spec:
  clusterIP: None
  selector:
    app: cache
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: cache
spec:
  serviceName: cache-svc
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cache
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cache
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: seed
        image: busybox
        command: ["sh", "-c", "echo seed > /data/.seed"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
      containers:
      - name: cache
        image: redis:7
        ports:
        - containerPort: 6379
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "512Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: "/ready", port: 6379}
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet: {path: "/live", port: 6379}
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: cache-pvc
  volumeClaimTemplates:
  - metadata:
      name: cache
    spec:
      accessModes: ["ReadWriteOnce"]
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: cache-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cache
```

Why This Is Asked
- Validates CKAD basics: Jobs, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, probes in a practical data-migrate flow.
- Introduces idempotence with a marker, a common real-world concern.

Key Concepts
- Job lifecycle and completion guarantees
- InitContainer usage for tooling installation
- Runtime config from ConfigMaps and Secrets
- PVC-based idempotence markers and backoff settings
- Probes and minimal YAML scaffolding

Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Job skeleton (pseudo)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: data-migrate
spec:
  backoffLimit: 3
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: csvkit-install
        image: alpine:latest
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache python3 py3-pip && pip3 install csvkit"]
      containers:
      - name: migrator
        image: curlimages/curl:7.88.0
        command: ["sh", "-c", "python3 migrate.py"]
        env:
        - name: MIG_BATCH_SIZE
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: mig-config
              key: MIG_BATCH_SIZE
        - name: API_TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: mig-creds
              key: api-token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data/migrate
        - name: marker
          mountPath: /data/marker
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: migrate-pvc
      - name: marker
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: migrate-marker-pvc
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      # probes would be defined on the migrator container
```

Follow-up Questions
- How would you test idempotence across retries?
- How would you handle partial CSV failures and ensure exactly-once semantics?

Tests basic CKAD concepts: PVC-backed watches, policy-driven validation, InitContainers, Secrets, sidecars, network policies, and external API reporting.

## Key Concepts

- Deployment, PVC, ConfigMap, Secret
- YAML validation with yq/jq; policy-driven checks
- InitContainer and TLS-sidecar patterns
- NetworkPolicy egress controls; readiness/liveness probes

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal skeleton: policy-watcher Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: policy-watcher
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: pods-pvc
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: pods-pvc
      - name: policies
        configMap:
          name: policy-config
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:3.19
        command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache yq jq"]
      containers:
      - name: watcher
        image: <registry>/policy-watcher:latest
        envFrom:
        - secretRef:
            name: api-creds
        volumeMounts:
        - name: pods-pvc
          mountPath: /pods
        - name: policies
          mountPath: /policies
```

- How would you test this in CI for policy regressions?
- What happens when policy-config changes at runtime?

## Why This Is Asked

Static-site serving in a per-namespace context tests PVC/ConfigMap/Secret integration, nginx config via ConfigMap, and safe multi-tenant limits with quotas and limits.

## Key Concepts

- Deployments, replicas, and rolling updates
- PVCs for shared data, ConfigMaps for content and nginx.conf, Secrets for credentials
- nginx basic auth integration via config map
- ClusterIP Service exposure and Readiness/Liveness probes
- Namespace ResourceQuota and LimitRange for multi-tenant safety

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal skeleton showing core resources
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: site-content
data:
  index.html: |-
    <html>...</html>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: nginx-config
data:
  nginx.conf: |
    server { listen 80; location / { auth_basic "Restricted"; auth_basic_user_file /etc/nginx/.htpasswd; root /usr/share/nginx/html; } }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: basic-auth
type: Opaque
data:
  # base64(encoded username:password)
  htpasswd: <base64>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: static-site
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:stable
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        volumeMounts:
        - name: site
          mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
        - name: config
          mountPath: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
          subPath: nginx.conf
        - name: auth
          mountPath: /etc/nginx/.htpasswd
          subPath: htpasswd
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
      volumes:
      - name: site
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: static-site-pvc
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: nginx-config
      - name: auth
        secret:
          secretName: basic-auth
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: static-site-svc
spec:
  selector:
    app: static-site
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 80
    protocol: TCP
  type: ClusterIP
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: static-site-pvc
spec:
  accessModes:
  - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you update content without downtime?
- How would you rotate credentials and reflect it in nginx without redeploying pods?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests RBAC scoping, CronJob scheduling, and in-cluster data backup to a ConfigMap without leaking secrets.

## Key Concepts
- RBAC granularity scoped to a namespace
- CronJob scheduling and Job templates
- Reading Kubernetes events via API in-cluster
- Updating/creating a ConfigMap from a Job

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: events-backup-sa
  namespace: metrics
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: events-backup-role
  namespace: metrics
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["events"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps"]
  verbs: ["get","update","create","patch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: events-backup-binding
  namespace: metrics
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: events-backup-role
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: events-backup-sa
  namespace: metrics
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: events-backup
  namespace: metrics
spec:
  schedule: "*/2 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: events-backup-sa
          containers:
          - name: backup
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh","-c","kubectl get events -n metrics -o json | jq '.items[0:50]' > /backup/events.json; kubectl create configmap events-backup --from-file=events.json=/backup/events.json -n metrics --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          volumes:
          - name: backup
            emptyDir: {}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor the ConfigMap growth and avoid hitting 1MiConfigMap limit?
- How would you rollback if the CronJob misbehaves or RBAC scope expands unintentionally?

## Why This Is Asked
Startup probes are essential for CKAD candidates to handle slow-start scenarios without penalizing pod readiness during initialization. This tests understanding of probe interactions, rollout reliability, and operational rollback strategies.

## Key Concepts
- startupProbe vs readinessProbe and livenessProbe orchestration
- TCP socket probing for service availability
- Pod rollout behavior with configurable thresholds
- Resource management and safe rollback procedures

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: collector
  namespace: ingest
spec:
  replicas: 2
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: collector
          image: collector:latest
          startupProbe:
            tcpSocket:
              port: 8080
            initialDelaySeconds: 30
            periodSeconds: 5
            timeoutSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 12
          readinessProbe:
            # Existing configuration preserved
          livenessProbe:
            # Existing configuration preserved
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 128Mi
            limits:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 512Mi
```

## Verification Strategy
Deploy with `kubectl apply -f` and monitor rollout with `kubectl rollout status deployment/collector -n ingest`. Verify startup behavior under load using `kubectl exec` to simulate traffic during initialization. Test rollback with `kubectl rollout undo deployment/collector -n ingest` if startup times exceed thresholds.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD proficiency across namespace-scoped automation, ConfigMap manipulation, InitContainers, and secure egress controls in real-world migration workflows.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob scoped to a namespace with per-namespace behavior
- InitContainer to install tooling (yq) and prepare environment
- ConfigMap-driven migration plan and idempotent updates
- PVC-backed logs and a Secret-backed external POST
- Readiness/Liveness probes for resilient Jobs
- Namespace NetworkPolicy to restrict egress to the migration portal

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton: per-namespace CronJob migrating ConfigMaps
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: config-migrate
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  schedule: "0 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: migrate-sa
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: alpine:3.17
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache go && go install github.com/mikefarah/yq@latest"]
          containers:
          - name: migrate
            image: my-registry/config-migrate:latest
            envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: migration-api
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            readinessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              httpGet:
                path: /healthz
                port: 8080
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: logs-pvc
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you ensure idempotent migrations across runs?
- How would you handle partial failures or large numbers of ConfigMaps?
- What monitoring would you add to detect drift or failures?
